title: SPiRaL-inspired multiresolution VTI ray-tracing forward model
summary: Trace synthetic 3-D tessellated source-receiver rays through VTI cells, apply group/slowness correction to Christoffel phase speeds, emit traces and material anisotropy checks, and generalize across coarse and refined meshes.

inputFiles.name: VTI benchmark instance
inputFiles.description: Three visible synthetic layered ray paths with lengths, angles, VTI speeds and Thomsen delta.

inputFiles.name: Scientific specification
inputFiles.description: Christoffel matrix, units, output schemas, invariants, and solver CLI contract.

referenceFiles.name: Evaluator reference
referenceFiles.description: Oracle values for visible and hidden fixtures; evaluator-only.

referenceFiles.name: Hidden changed instance A
referenceFiles.description: Evaluator-only refined ray geometry and material values.

referenceFiles.name: Hidden changed instance B
referenceFiles.description: Evaluator-only coarse/fine multiresolution domain with independent materials.

taskPrompt:
You are implementing a synthetic 3-D tessellated source-receiver ray-tracing workflow inspired by the SPiRaL global tomography model. Read input/spec.md completely.

Read input/problem.json and implement the VTI Christoffel qP/qSV/qSH phase calculation plus the specified support/stationary group-slowness maximization for oblique geometric rays. Produce output/result.json, output/trace.csv, and output/solver.py. The solver.py must be reusable and runnable as `python solver.py --input PATH --result PATH --trace PATH`; it must use only the Python standard library and work for arbitrary conforming coarse/fine tessellations.

Your result.json must contain exactly schema_version, visible, and invariant (v2). Preserve ray and tessellated-cell order. The CSV header and row schema in spec.md are exact. Check finite values, qP >= qSV, and material xi=(Vsh/Vsv)^2. Do not modify input/. Do not use internet, NumPy, SciPy, or hard-coded visible answers. The evaluator independently reruns your solver on two changed hidden meshes and recomputes every eigenvalue and group slowness.
agentMustDo: Derive the TI stiffness terms, 2x2 Christoffel eigenvalues, and support/stationary group slowness from input/spec.md.
Implement a reusable solver.py CLI and run it on the visible instance.
Emit exact JSON and CSV schemas, including an intermediate per-segment trace and invariant fields.
Validate units, ray/group correction, material xi and eigenvalue ordering; do not hard-code visible values.
evaluation: Hard gates reject missing/malformed/oversized files, extra JSON keys, wrong CSV headers/rows, non-finite values, forbidden imports, or failed solver CLI. Weighted score: 0.45 visible travel times/xi, 0.20 trace, 0.15 physical invariants, 0.20 hidden solver recomputation. The hidden component independently recomputes all trace physics from two changed fixtures and is required for a high score.
